title: 🧮🎨🧠Synesthesia: Blending the Senses to Distill the Soul

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: It's Joel Blackstock with the Taproot Therapy Collective podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我是 Joel Blackstock，欢迎收听 Taproot Therapy Collective 播客。

sentences.en: And today, we're going to be reading an article called Synesthesia,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要读一篇文章，题目叫《联觉：

sentences.en: Blending the Senses to Distill the Soul.
sentences.zh: 融合感官，萃取灵魂》。

sentences.en: Now, before we begin our discussion of synesthesia, or we even define it if you don't know what it is,
sentences.zh: 在开始讨论联觉，或者如果你不知道它是什么，甚至在定义它之前，

sentences.en: we're going to consider this passage from a book called The Peregrine, which is one of my favorite books.
sentences.zh: 我们先来看看《游隼》这本书中的一段话，这是我最喜欢的书之一。

sentences.en: It is a bird-watching journal of a naturalist, which sounds boring as hell, but it is beautiful, and it is a lot more than it seeMs. As Werner Herzog pointed out in his review,
sentences.zh: 这是一位博物学家的观鸟日记，听起来枯燥透顶，但它非常优美，而且远不止表面看起来那么简单。正如 Werner Herzog 在书评中指出的，

sentences.en: it is not a book about a person who is watching a bird.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一本关于某人观察鸟类的书。

sentences.en: It is about a person who is wanting to and maybe becoming a bird.
sentences.zh: 它是关于一个人渴望成为鸟，甚至可能正在变成鸟的故事。

sentences.en: But anyway, this is not a review of The Peregrine.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，这并不是《游隼》的书评。

sentences.en: It is an article on synesthesia, so I'm going to begin that reading from this book now.
sentences.zh: 这是一篇关于联觉的文章，所以我现在要开始从这本书中进行朗读。

sentences.en: The first bird that I searched for was the night jar, which used to nest in the valley.
sentences.zh: 我寻找的第一种鸟是夜鹰，它过去常在山谷里筑巢。

sentences.en: Its song is like the sound of a stream of wine spilling out from a height into a deep and booming cask of wood.
sentences.zh: 它的歌声就像一股葡萄酒从高处倾泻而下，注入深邃而轰鸣的木桶中。

sentences.en: It is an odorous sound with a bouquet that rises to the quiet sky.
sentences.zh: 这是一种带有芬芳的声音，香气升腾至宁静的天空。

sentences.en: In the glare of day, it would seem thinner and drier, but dusk mellow it and give it vintage.
sentences.zh: 在白昼的强光下，它显得稀薄而干燥，但黄昏使它变得醇厚，赋予它陈年的韵味。

sentences.en: If a song could smell, this song would smell of crushed grape and almond and dark wood.
sentences.zh: 如果歌声有气味，这歌声闻起来就像压碎的葡萄、杏仁和深色木材的味道。

sentences.en: The sound spills out and none of it is loSt. The whole wood brims with it and then stops.
sentences.zh: 声音倾泻而出，没有一丝流失。整个树林都充盈着它，然后戛然而止。

sentences.en: Suddenly, unexpectedly, but the ear hears it.
sentences.zh: 突然，出乎意料，但耳朵听到了。

sentences.en: Still, a prolonged and fading echo, draining and winding out among the surrounding trees into the deep stillness.
sentences.zh: 依然，那是一阵悠长而渐弱的回响，在周围的树木间流淌、蜿蜒，汇入深沉的寂静。

sentences.en: Between the early stars and the long afterglow, the nightjar leaps up joyfully.
sentences.zh: 在初升的星辰与漫长的余晖之间，夜鹰欢快地跃起。

sentences.en: It glides and flutters, dances, bounces, lightly and silently away.
sentences.zh: 它滑翔、扑动、舞蹈、弹跳，轻盈而无声地远去。

sentences.en: Sparrowhawks were always near me in the dusk, like something I meant but could never quite remember.
sentences.zh: 黄昏时分，雀鹰总是在我身边，就像某种我想要表达却永远无法完全记起的东西。

sentences.en: So let's sit for a minute with a couple things going on in that passage.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们花点时间来细细品味这段文字中的几个要点。

sentences.en: And you can speculate on why I might include it in an article about synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 你们可以推测一下，为什么我会把它收录进一篇关于联觉的文章里。

sentences.en: Oh, I lost my mic.
sentences.zh: 哦，我的麦克风掉了。

sentences.en: Okay, there we go.
sentences.zh: 好了，没问题了。

sentences.en: So let's look at the things that is going on in this passage.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看这段文字中到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: So in the glare of day, it would seem thinner and drier, but dusk mellow it and give it vintage.
sentences.zh: 在白昼的强光下，它显得稀薄而干燥，但黄昏使它变得醇厚，赋予它陈年的韵味。

sentences.en: So the sound is being compared to the visual of a wine pouring into a cask.
sentences.zh: 所以，声音被比作葡萄酒倒入木桶的视觉画面。

sentences.en: You also have him saying that the air and the quality of light change the way that the ear hears sound.
sentences.zh: 他还提到空气和光线的质量改变了耳朵听到的声音方式。

sentences.en: The stream of wine spilling from a height into a deep and booming cask.
sentences.zh: 一股葡萄酒从高处倾泻而下，注入深邃而轰鸣的木桶中。

sentences.en: He describes the sound as having a smell and the smell changing based on the color and the texture of light in the air.
sentences.zh: 他描述声音具有气味，而且气味会随着空气中光线的颜色和质感而改变。

sentences.en: The ear hears it and still a prolonged and fading echo, draining and winding out among the surrounding trees.
sentences.zh: 耳朵听到了，依然是一阵悠长而渐弱的回响，在周围的树木间流淌、蜿蜒。

sentences.en: Or the ear hears it still.
sentences.zh: 或者说，耳朵依然听到了它。

sentences.en: Sorry, I'm not going to read the whole passage again.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我不会再读一遍全文了。

sentences.en: But the perception of sound in the inner world of the mind endures after the sensation of sound in the outer world has ended.
sentences.zh: 但在心灵的内在世界中，对声音的感知在外部世界的声音感觉结束后依然存在。

sentences.en: It's implied because of a visual, because of what he's looking at.
sentences.zh: 这是因为视觉，因为他所看到的东西而暗示出来的。

sentences.en: So what we're getting here is all of these senses blending together, or not blending
sentences.zh: 所以我们在这里看到的是所有这些感官融合在一起，或者说并没有融合

sentences.en: together, which is I think how we think of synesthesia too often, but the senses are influencing
sentences.zh: 在一起，我认为我们对联觉的理解往往过于简单，但感官确实在相互

sentences.en: each other and he is perceiving the way that they influence one another and describing it beautifully.
sentences.zh: 影响，他感知到了它们相互影响的方式，并进行了优美的描述。

sentences.en: We don't know a whole lot about the author of the Peregrine if you haven't listened to it.
sentences.zh: 如果你没听过《游隼》的作者，我们对他了解并不多。

sentences.en: It's a short read.
sentences.zh: 这是一本短篇读物。

sentences.en: It's a short audible.
sentences.zh: 这是一本短篇有声书。

sentences.en: The narration on the audible I actually really like.
sentences.zh: 我其实非常喜欢有声书里的旁白。

sentences.en: It does the original justice.
sentences.zh: 它忠实于原著。

sentences.en: We don't know a ton about the author other than he watched birds, a lot of the poison that was in the air at that time.
sentences.zh: 除了他观察鸟类，以及当时空气中存在大量毒素之外，我们对他了解不多。

sentences.en: Pesticides were killing the Peregrine, so he thought likely it would not be alive.
sentences.zh: 杀虫剂正在杀死游隼，所以他认为游隼可能活不长了。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 但它还活着。

sentences.en: It hasn't gone extinct.
sentences.zh: 它并没有灭绝。

sentences.en: He thought it would not be alive much past his life.
sentences.zh: 他认为游隼活不过他的余生。

sentences.en: And we also know that he was probably suffering from some kind of illness that was probably lethal and probably what killed him.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道他可能患有某种致命的疾病，这很可能就是他的死因。

sentences.en: Other than that, we don't really know a lot other than his house, which is still there.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，除了他的房子还在那里，我们真的了解不多。

sentences.en: That's an interesting story.
sentences.zh: 那是一个有趣的故事。

sentences.en: If you want to look up the Peregrine, we're going to continue on with this article about synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 如果你想去查查《游隼》，我们现在继续讲这篇关于联觉的文章。

sentences.en: So we know that we can't see sound and we know that we can't taste it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们看不见声音，也尝不出它的味道。

sentences.en: How does this podcast taste?
sentences.zh: 这个播客是什么味道的？

sentences.en: You also can't smell it.
sentences.zh: 你也闻不到它。

sentences.en: How's my breath?
sentences.zh: 我的口气怎么样？

sentences.en: You know, this description of birdsong tickles our other senses, even though we know those things are not a logical one.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种对鸟鸣的描述触动了我们的其他感官，尽管我们知道这些描述在逻辑上并不成立。

sentences.en: They are not even an intuitive one, but a metaphor that is kind of, you know, deep in the mind.
sentences.zh: 它们甚至不是直觉上的，而是一种深植于心灵深处的隐喻。

sentences.en: It's not that it felt like this.
sentences.zh: 并不是说感觉像这样。

sentences.en: It's just that these things are each other.
sentences.zh: 而是这些事物本身就是彼此。

sentences.en: You know, you might hear style writers describe colors or patterns as loud, or food writers describe taste as shining or dull.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可能会听到风格作家将颜色或图案描述为“响亮”，或者美食作家将味道描述为“闪耀”或“沉闷”。

sentences.en: And this is obviously, this is a synesthetic association.
sentences.zh: 这显然是一种联觉联想。

sentences.en: And since the writers are not talking about the food's ability to reflect light or make noise, synesthesia is when the senses blend.
sentences.zh: 既然作家们谈论的不是食物反射光线或发出噪音的能力，那么联觉就是感官融合的时候。

sentences.en: It's a condition that is a medical term.
sentences.zh: 这是一种医学术语所指的病症。

sentences.en: And it's a fascinating phenomenon where the stimulation of one sensory or cognitive pathway triggers involuntarily another experience.
sentences.zh: 这是一种迷人的现象，即一个感官或认知途径的刺激会不由自主地触发另一种体验。

sentences.en: So, you know, a lot of times people will describe synesthesia as that they ate mushrooms, and then
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，很多时候人们会把联觉描述为他们吃了蘑菇，然后

sentences.en: that mushroom made them eat the color yellow, or smell what their friend was saying, or, you know, speak a vision or something.
sentences.zh: 那个蘑菇让他们吃到了黄色，或者闻到了朋友说话的味道，或者，你知道，说出了一种幻象之类的东西。

sentences.en: And it isn't always just one sense is being used the wrong way.
sentences.zh: 而且并不总是只有一种感官被错误地使用。

sentences.en: It is a deep commingling of the senses that is kind of profound.
sentences.zh: 这是一种深刻的感官交融，相当深奥。

sentences.en: And what I'm arguing in this article is not just, you know, a symptom, but it's actually experiencing of the way that the deep brain works
sentences.zh: 我在文章中要论证的不仅仅是一个症状，它实际上是体验大脑深层运作方式的一种途径，

sentences.en: before our brain filters and puts all this stuff back together.
sentences.zh: 在我们的思维进行过滤并把所有这些东西重新组合之前。

sentences.en: So synesthesia is, you know, when it's, it can be a bad symptom in some people that want to get rid of it.
sentences.zh: 所以联觉，你知道，在某些想要摆脱它的人身上，它可能是一种糟糕的症状。

sentences.en: But it also is not just a bad thing that is happening wrong.
sentences.zh: 但它也不仅仅是一件出了问题的坏事。

sentences.en: It is kind of us getting a little peek into the perception of the deep brain.
sentences.zh: 它更像是让我们窥探到了大脑深层的感知。

sentences.en: And so, you know, there's a cousin of Charles Darwin, and he coins the term synesthesia, and he begins documenting various cases.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，查尔斯·达尔文有一位表亲，他创造了“联觉”这个词，并开始记录各种病例。

sentences.en: But it is a very old phenomenon in our psyche.
sentences.zh: 但这在我们人类心理中是一种非常古老的现象。

sentences.en: You know, synesthetic experiences, they've left traces throughout human history.
sentences.zh: 你知道，联觉体验在人类历史上留下了痕迹。

sentences.en: So we know that this is something that goes back a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道这是一种由来已久的东西。

sentences.en: It's definitely not invented in Darwin's time.
sentences.zh: 它绝对不是在达尔文时代才发明的。

sentences.en: And manifesting, you know, they show up in ancient mythology, art, and religious practices.
sentences.zh: 它表现出来，你知道，出现在古代神话、艺术和宗教实践中。

sentences.en: So the concept of rasa, for example, in Indian aesthetic philosophy associates emotion with specific colors, taste and musical tones.
sentences.zh: 例如，印度美学哲学中的“味”（Rasa）概念，将情感与特定的颜色、味道和音乐音调联系起来。

sentences.en: For example, the emotion of love is often associated with the color red, or the taste of sweet, with certain kinds of round musical tone.
sentences.zh: 例如，爱的感觉通常与红色、甜味以及某种圆润的音乐音调相关联。

sentences.en: And in the
sentences.zh: 而在

sentences.en: Greek world, the poet Sappho, there's a lot of references to synesthetic experience in her work and a lot of other Greek work in Latin.
sentences.zh: 希腊世界，诗人萨福的作品中有很多关于联觉体验的引用，在其他希腊和拉丁作品中也是如此。

sentences.en: For one, you know, Sappho writes, as I listen, the faint scent of lemon trees rises in the sound of your voice.
sentences.zh: 首先，你知道，萨福写道：当我倾听时，柠檬树的淡淡清香在你的声音中升起。

sentences.en: The poems of the Persian poet Rumi, who is a mystic that I like a lot, they often employ a synesthetic language that describes a spiritual experience.
sentences.zh: 波斯诗人鲁米的诗歌，他是我非常喜欢的一位神秘主义者，经常使用描述精神体验的联觉语言。

sentences.en: For example, Rumi writes, the flute of the infinite is played without ceasing, and its sound is love.
sentences.zh: 例如，鲁米写道：无限的笛声不停地吹奏，它的声音就是爱。

sentences.en: Whoever hears this sound merges into it.
sentences.zh: 凡听到这声音的人，都会融入其中。

sentences.en: In the Bible, you also have a synesthetic description.
sentences.zh: 在《圣经》中，也有联觉的描述。

sentences.en: Taste and see that the Lord is good.
sentences.zh: 你们要尝尝主恩的滋味，便知道他是美善。

sentences.en: This is, you know, probably not telling you to eat
sentences.zh: 这，你知道，可能不是在让你去吃

sentences.en: God.
sentences.zh: 上帝。

sentences.en: Here, the act of tasting is metaphorically linked with this experience of the goodness of
sentences.zh: 在这里，品尝的行为被隐喻性地与这种对上帝美善的体验，

sentences.en: God, or the flavor of God.
sentences.zh: 或者说上帝的滋味联系在了一起。

sentences.en: And these ancient poets use these synesthetic-like associations to enhance this transcendental effect of their writing, as we still use it today.
sentences.zh: 这些古代诗人利用这些类似联觉的联想来增强他们写作的超验效果，就像我们今天依然在使用它一样。

sentences.en: You feel something a little bit different than if I was like, I saw a bird, the bird went in the sky, the bird had wings, the bird ate a worm.
sentences.zh: 你感觉到的东西，和你听我说“我看到一只鸟，鸟飞向天空，鸟有翅膀，鸟吃了一条虫子”是完全不同的。

sentences.en: That is, you know, not what the peregrine is.
sentences.zh: 那，你知道，不是《游隼》所表达的内容。

sentences.en: The Hindu philosophy of chakras points, you know, it posits that there's this association and cross-activation between somatic experiences in different parts of the body.
sentences.zh: 印度教的脉轮哲学指出，你知道，它假设身体不同部位的躯体体验之间存在这种关联和交叉激活。

sentences.en: So chakras have a physical location in the body, like a somatic association, an emotional association, and then also a color.
sentences.zh: 所以脉轮在身体上有物理位置，比如躯体关联、情感关联，还有颜色。

sentences.en: And then in other kinds of practice, there's also a link between different kinds of energy or sound frequency.
sentences.zh: 而在其他类型的实践中，不同类型的能量或声音频率之间也存在联系。

sentences.en: So they're kind of saying that like this sort of sound evokes this kind of emotion, that emotion is stored in this place in
sentences.zh: 所以他们是在说，这种声音唤起了这种情绪，这种情绪在身体中以物理方式存储在某个位置，

sentences.en: the body physically, and the body is also responding to this kind of color.
sentences.zh: 而且身体也会对这种颜色做出反应。

sentences.en: So it's, you know, it is this kind of deep synesthetic, you know, fusion of senses that was used in ancient medicine, and still today by some people.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是一种深刻的联觉，你知道，感官的融合，被古代医学所使用，今天仍被一些人使用。

sentences.en: Chakras, you know, could have provided our ancestors with this framework to understand and regulate their physical and emotional well-being.
sentences.zh: 脉轮，你知道，可能为我们的祖先提供了一个理解和调节他们身心健康的框架。

sentences.en: You know, when they felt bad, they knew that if they went and they recognized the emotion of, well, what is it?
sentences.zh: 你知道，当他们感觉不好时，他们知道如果他们去识别那种情绪，嗯，那是什么？

sentences.en: It's anger.
sentences.zh: 是愤怒。

sentences.en: I'm going to look at red.
sentences.zh: 我要看红色。

sentences.en: I'm going to feel this here.
sentences.zh: 我要在这里感受它。

sentences.en: I'm going to have this sound.
sentences.zh: 我要有这种声音。

sentences.en: You know, there was this way of kind of recognizing and regulating and rebalancing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种识别、调节和重新平衡的方式。

sentences.en: So, you know, by linking specific emotions and bodily sensations to different energy centers represented by chakras,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，通过将特定的情绪和身体感觉与脉轮所代表的不同能量中心联系起来，

sentences.en: the individuals in the past might have been able to identify and address imbalances in their physical and emotional states.
sentences.zh: 过去的人们可能已经能够识别并解决他们身心状态中的失衡。

sentences.en: So the color association with chakras may also have served as this visual aid to enhance the focus and awareness of these energy centers during meditation and spiritual practice.
sentences.zh: 所以脉轮的颜色联想也可能作为一种视觉辅助，在冥想和精神实践中增强对这些能量中心的关注和觉知。

sentences.en: You know, colors have a very strong psychological and physiological effect on individuals and using specific colors and association with chakras might have facilitated a
sentences.zh: 你知道，颜色对个人有非常强烈的心理和生理影响，使用特定的颜色并与脉轮联系起来，可能促进了

sentences.en: deeper connection with activation of these energy centers.
sentences.zh: 与这些能量中心激活的更深层联系。

sentences.en: You know, synesthesia may have helped shaman and philosophers, you know, perceive these sensory associations.
sentences.zh: 你知道，联觉可能帮助过萨满和哲学家，你知道，感知这些感官联想。

sentences.en: Like they were intuitive people.
sentences.zh: 就像他们是直觉敏锐的人。

sentences.en: They could kind of get underneath cognition and experience it in a way that was a little bit more
sentences.zh: 他们可以深入认知之下，以一种更接近大脑底层的方式去体验它，

sentences.en: close to the bottom of the brain or, you know, more pure or more dissociated, whatever you want to call it.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，更纯粹或更解离，随你怎么称呼它。

sentences.en: And then when they took these realizations out of that transcendental state, they were able to use them to help other people who did not have that heightened perception heal.

sentences.zh: 这真的很疯狂。

sentences.zh: 所以你看不见它。

sentences.zh: 所以你看到的一些东西完全是大脑编造出来的，而且，你知道，它恰好是正确的，呃，

sentences.en: because, uh, you know, we rely on it and we don't perceive that.
sentences.zh: 因为，呃，我们依赖它，而我们并没有察觉到这一点。

sentences.en: Um, so, you know, that information is being processed, but it's not being perceived, but there's a ton of information
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你知道，这些信息正在被处理，但并没有被感知，但大脑层面上有大量的信息

sentences.en: that's going on on the space level of the brain that you don't have access to.
sentences.zh: 正在发生，而你是无法获取的。

sentences.zh: 比如，我不能坐在这里说，你知道，我的呼吸会停止，你知道，如果我等一分钟，我就不会注意到

sentences.zh: 我在呼吸，然后我可以思考它，说，好吧，现在我得记得呼吸，直到我再次忘记它。

sentences.en: Then my body takes that over, but I can't sit here and then say, okay, I'm going to, uh, try and perceive all the blood vessels and blind spots on

sentences.zh: 把那东西拆开，感知眼睛传来的不同视频流。

sentences.en: And then like, I can't do that.
sentences.zh: 然后，我做不到。

sentences.en: Like you can't.
sentences.zh: 就像你做不到一样。

sentences.en: So, you know, the closest thing that you can do is something called prisoner cinema, where if you close your eyes and you look at the blackness behind your eyes,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你能做的最接近的事情就是所谓的“囚徒电影”（prisoner cinema），如果你闭上眼睛，看着眼前的黑暗，

sentences.en: there'll be all these sort of visual tricks that the processing does.
sentences.zh: 会有各种各样的视觉把戏，那是大脑处理过程产生的。

sentences.en: And you'll see little blue sparks or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你会看到蓝色的小火花之类的东西。

sentences.en: Um, and, but you know, I'm going into the woods, but you know, our brain doesn't show us all of the chaos that it is processing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是你知道，我扯远了，但你知道，我们的大脑并没有向我们展示它正在处理的所有混乱。

sentences.en: It only shows us what we need to be able to perceive ourself in the world around us.
sentences.zh: 它只向我们展示我们需要感知自身和周围世界所需的东西。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that there's not information in that processing where the senses are kind of blending and influencing one another.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着在处理过程中没有信息，感官在某种程度上是混合并相互影响的。

sentences.en: Um, and, and things like brain spawning or ETT, you know, color-based therapies, they're sort of hijacking
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有像脑点法（Brainspotting）或ETT（情绪转化疗法）这样的东西，你知道，基于颜色的疗法，它们是在劫持

sentences.en: those visual glitches in the brain in order to get trauma out of the body.
sentences.zh: 大脑中的那些视觉故障，以便将创伤从身体中释放出来。

sentences.en: So, you know, this, in, in individuals that have schizophrenia, um, you know, there, there's, uh, abnormalities in the brain, sensory gating.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在患有精神分裂症的个体中，嗯，你知道，大脑的感官门控存在异常。

sentences.en: You know, we, we used to think that we, we, it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们过去认为我们……这不重要。

sentences.en: I'm not going into the history of that.
sentences.zh: 我不会深入探讨那段历史。

sentences.en: We used to have different theories about schizophrenia, but the common one now that sort of replaced those is that there's a sensory gating mechanism.
sentences.zh: 我们过去对精神分裂症有不同的理论，但现在取代那些理论的普遍观点是，存在一种感官门控机制。

sentences.en: It's not that the brain is making something up.
sentences.zh: 并不是大脑在编造什么。

sentences.en: Um, it's actually that it isn't filtering something out that everybody else has, you know, this ability to discard all this information, but a person with schizophrenia,
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上是它没有过滤掉某些东西，而其他人都有这种丢弃所有这些信息的能力，但精神分裂症患者，

sentences.en: they can't tell it apart.
sentences.zh: 他们无法区分。

sentences.en: Um, and when I used to work with people, well, I still work with some people that have schizophrenia, but when I used to work only people only that had schizophrenia, um, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我过去和人们一起工作时，好吧，我现在仍然和一些患有精神分裂症的人一起工作，但当我过去只和精神分裂症患者一起工作时，嗯，你知道，

sentences.en: that was one of the things they would say is like, everything makes sense to me.
sentences.zh: 那是他们会说的一件事，就像，一切对我来说都有意义。

sentences.en: And then I say this new thing and that doesn't make sense to anybody.
sentences.zh: 然后我说出这个新东西，而这对任何人来说都没有意义。

sentences.en: And they couldn't tell the difference in between what they were, you know, inventing eventually, essentially, and what everyone else assumed,
sentences.zh: 他们无法区分他们本质上是在“发明”什么，以及其他人认为什么是现实，

sentences.en: you know, their reality was, you know, 90% the same as everyone else's reality.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们的现实有90%和别人的现实是一样的。

sentences.en: Um, but then, you know, 10%, it wasn't there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但然后，你知道，那10%是不存在的。

sentences.en: And that's sort of true of everybody.
sentences.zh: 这对每个人来说都是一样的。

sentences.en: We don't all live in the same perceived world, but we kind of know what things are mine.
sentences.zh: 我们并非都生活在同一个感知的世界里，但我们多少知道哪些事情是属于我的。

sentences.en: You know, there's certain, uh, you know, hobbies or ideas that I wouldn't just say on the podcaSt. Cause they, you know, they may not be,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些爱好或想法我不会在播客上说，因为它们，你知道，它们可能不是……

sentences.en: you know, I would know that they may be inflammatory or something where somebody else, they don't have that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我会知道它们可能具有煽动性，或者别人没有那种顾虑。

sentences.en: And it's not that their brain is making up something.
sentences.zh: 并不是他们的大脑在编造什么。

sentences.en: It's that it isn't filtering things out.
sentences.zh: 而是它没有过滤掉某些东西。

sentences.en: Um, and a lot of delusion is active imagination, um, or, uh, wish fulfillment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，很多妄想是主动想象，嗯，或者是愿望满足。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of psychosis is this, uh, unconscious creative process that is making things that are not being labeled as made up or not being discarded.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多精神病是这种无意识的创造过程，它制造出的东西没有被标记为“编造”，也没有被丢弃。

sentences.en: Um, and so the sensory gating theory of schizophrenia, I think explains a whole lot, um, about the thesis of what I'm trying to say
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以精神分裂症的感官门控理论，我认为解释了很多，嗯，关于我想表达的论点，

sentences.en: about the way that's synesthesia works in the brain.
sentences.zh: 关于联觉在大脑中是如何运作的。

sentences.en: And so, um, you know, creativity and intuition and humans, um, might be caused by gaps in these sensory gates that allow for unorthodox ways of
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，你知道，人类的创造力和直觉，嗯，可能是由这些感官门控的间隙引起的，这些间隙允许非正统的方式

sentences.en: information being processed that end up to be useful.
sentences.zh: 处理信息，最终证明是有用的。

sentences.en: You know, most evolutionary advantages start off as an accident and then they're useful.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大多数进化优势最初都是偶然的，然后才变得有用。

sentences.en: So they stick around.
sentences.zh: 所以它们保留了下来。

sentences.en: Um, you know, you get too much of it and then it becomes a problem again.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，如果太多了，它又会变成一个问题。

sentences.en: Uh, for example, you know, sickle cell anemia, the reason that that exists is that, um, people who have the recessive gene for sickle cell anemia, they don't get malaria.
sentences.zh: 呃，例如，你知道，镰状细胞贫血，它存在的原因是，嗯，携带镰状细胞贫血隐性基因的人，他们不会得疟疾。

sentences.en: Um, the blood cell can't get, uh, messed with by this disease, but you have too much of it when you get the dominant one.
sentences.zh: 嗯，血细胞不会被这种疾病破坏，但当你获得显性基因时，你就有了太多这种细胞。

sentences.en: All of a sudden the, this shape of the cell is not different enough to protect you from the virus.
sentences.zh: 突然间，这种细胞的形状不足以保护你免受病毒侵害。

sentences.en: It is so different that it can no longer go through your veins and you're in a ton of pain.
sentences.zh: 它太不同了，以至于无法再通过你的静脉，你会感到剧烈的疼痛。

sentences.en: Um, and so, you know, these
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你知道，这些

sentences.en: small, um, genetic predispositions to have an imperfect sensory gate, um, you know, they probably,
sentences.zh: 微小的、嗯，导致感官门控不完美的遗传倾向，嗯，你知道，它们可能，

sentences.en: uh, are part of what give us this ability to be creative and intuitive, um, especially in certain people.
sentences.zh: 呃，是我们获得这种创造力和直觉能力的一部分，嗯，特别是在某些人身上。

sentences.en: And then even in everybody, you know, everybody's brain can be plastic up to a point.
sentences.zh: 而且即使在每个人身上，你知道，每个人的大脑在一定程度上都是可塑的。

sentences.en: So like if you start to concentrate on these things and practice creativity and practice intuition and
sentences.zh: 所以如果你开始专注于这些事情，练习创造力，练习直觉，并

sentences.en: practice mindfulness, then yeah, you start to perceive deeper and deeper layers of the mind.
sentences.zh: 练习正念，那么是的，你开始感知到心灵越来越深层的层面。

sentences.en: Um, and so it would make sense that people who do those practices have better access to these things that sound a lot like schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以那些进行这些练习的人能更好地接触到这些听起来很像精神分裂症的东西，这是有道理的。

sentences.en: You know, it's, it's long been speculated that schizophrenia might just be this overabundance or overexpression of the same genes that lead to
sentences.zh: 你知道，长期以来人们一直猜测，精神分裂症可能只是导致

sentences.en: creativity or new perspectives and new ideas.
sentences.zh: 创造力或新视角和新想法的相同基因的过度丰富或过度表达。

sentences.en: Creativity and intuition can help us see how to color outside the lines.
sentences.zh: 创造力和直觉可以帮助我们看到如何跳出框框思考。

sentences.en: But when there's too many of those tendencies, uh, to break rules, then we can't see the lines at all.
sentences.zh: 但当有太多那种打破规则的倾向时，我们就根本看不到框框了。

sentences.en: Um, we don't even know that we're coloring outside of the lines.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们甚至不知道我们正在跳出框框。

sentences.en: You know, Joseph Campbell used to say that the artist swims in the ocean that this, the person with schizophrenia drowns it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，约瑟夫·坎贝尔（Joseph Campbell）过去常说，艺术家在海洋中游泳，而精神分裂症患者在其中溺水。

sentences.en: I think he actually said schizophrenic, but that's not person, patient centered language.
sentences.zh: 我想他实际上说的是“精神分裂症患者”（schizophrenic），但这不符合以人为本、以患者为中心的语言。

sentences.en: You can't say that anymore.
sentences.zh: 你不能再那样说了。

sentences.en: Um, it's, you know, person with homelessness, not a homeless person.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是，你知道，患有无家可归的人，而不是无家可归者。

sentences.en: It's person with schizophrenia, um, which is the right way to say it.
sentences.zh: 是患有精神分裂症的人，嗯，这是正确的说法。

sentences.en: Um, but I'm just reading a quote.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我只是在读一段引语。

sentences.en: So if I change it, I want to explain why.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我改动它，我想解释原因。

sentences.en: So anyway, he meant there that the deep layers of the unconscious can enrich us.
sentences.zh: 总之，他的意思是无意识的深层可以丰富我们。

sentences.en: But if we go too deep, then we can lose ourselves.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们走得太深，那么我们可能会迷失自我。

sentences.en: You know, Jung said that the ego has to go down into the unconscious, but if it goes down over and over too deep, then it loses its ability to have any kind of rigidity at all.
sentences.zh: 你知道，荣格说自我必须深入到无意识中，但如果它一次又一次地深入太深，那么它就会失去任何僵硬的能力。

sentences.en: And no longer is it too rigid.
sentences.zh: 它不再是太僵硬了。

sentences.en: It isn't able to be rigid enough to keep the unconscious out.
sentences.zh: 它无法保持足够的僵硬来将无意识挡在外面。

sentences.en: Um, so, you know, our senses are not as distinct as we would like to make them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你知道，我们的感官并不像我们想要的那样清晰。

sentences.en: You know, we think about senses in this ordered way that the ear hears sound and the brain perceives the sound, but that's not really how the brain works.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们以这种有序的方式思考感官，耳朵听到声音，大脑感知声音，但这并不是大脑真正的工作方式。

sentences.en: All of our senses are blended together and they send messages to our body and emotional system before the brainstem filters them for us, you know, to be able to feel them.
sentences.zh: 我们所有的感官都混合在一起，在脑干为我们过滤它们之前，它们就向我们的身体和情绪系统发送信息，你知道，为了能够感受到它们。

sentences.en: You know, all of our senses are blended together and the brain filters them for us.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们所有的感官都混合在一起，大脑为我们过滤它们。

sentences.en: And the ego consciousness and our self perception is really one of the smallest parts of who we are.
sentences.zh: 而自我意识和我们的自我感知实际上是我们身份中最小的部分之一。

sentences.en: We think it's all we are.
sentences.zh: 我们以为这就是我们的全部。

sentences.en: The ego wants to be all of who we are.
sentences.zh: 自我想要成为我们的全部。

sentences.en: Um, but our brain does an enormous amount of work before the sensations that we perceive are presented to our ego on the silver platter to perceive.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但在我们感知的感官被呈现在银盘上供自我感知之前，我们的大脑做了大量的工作。

sentences.en: And the keys to unlocking our psychology, I think, lie in understanding
sentences.zh: 我认为解锁我们心理学的关键在于理解

sentences.en: synesthesia and the spaghetti bowl mess of processing and perception that is taking place in our brain at any moment.
sentences.zh: 联觉以及大脑中随时都在发生的混乱的处理和感知过程。

sentences.en: You know, treatments like somatic therapy or emotional transformation therapy, which I got trained in in Texas last weekend to use color and light.
sentences.zh: 你知道，像躯体疗法或情绪转化疗法（ETT）这样的治疗方法，我上周末在德克萨斯州接受了使用颜色和光的培训。

sentences.en: Um, uh, it's an eye therapy like brain spotting, but it doesn't use position.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呃，这是一种像脑点法一样的眼部疗法，但它不使用位置。

sentences.en: It uses color and light.
sentences.zh: 它使用颜色和光。

sentences.en: Um, you can come in and see me and we'll do that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可以来找我，我们来做那个。

sentences.en: It's pretty wild.
sentences.zh: 这很疯狂。

sentences.en: And then, you know, what is down there, you know, I watched a piece of paper turn black in front of me that my eyes knew was blue.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，那下面有什么，你知道，我看着一张纸在我面前变黑，而我的眼睛知道它是蓝色的。

sentences.en: And it's like, I know this is blue.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我知道这是蓝色的。

sentences.en: What is going on?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: And I watched my eyes turn it black.
sentences.zh: 我看着我的眼睛把它变黑了。

sentences.en: Um, and that was because I had a traumatic association with one of the emotions that we were working with.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是因为我对我们正在处理的情绪之一有创伤性的联想。

sentences.en: And so, you know, older traditions like chakras and transcendental meditation, I mean, they're based on using utilizing these same glitches and perception.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，像脉轮和超觉冥想这样的古老传统，我的意思是，它们的基础是利用这些相同的感知故障。

sentences.en: And while brain spotting uses eye position, EMDR uses eye movement and ETT therapy uses color as a trigger to release trauma from the deep brain.
sentences.zh: 虽然脑点法使用眼睛位置，EMDR使用眼球运动，而ETT疗法使用颜色作为触发器来释放深层大脑的创伤。

sentences.en: And I'm sure there's other ways in there, um, to use the senses.
sentences.zh: 我相信还有其他方法，嗯，可以使用感官。

sentences.en: Um, but you know, uh, it's long been recognized that there's this powerful stimulus that can elicit emotion and psychological responses in humans, uh, within color.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但你知道，呃，长期以来人们一直公认，颜色中存在一种强大的刺激，能够引发人类的情绪和心理反应。

sentences.en: Uh, we disagree on exactly where that comes from or exactly what it is, but we know that color influences us.
sentences.zh: 呃，我们对于这种刺激的来源或本质究竟是什么尚存分歧，但我们知道颜色确实会影响我们。

sentences.en: You know, if, if it didn't at all, why would we have a preference about color when we bought clothes or painted our house?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果它完全没有影响，那为什么我们在买衣服或粉刷房子时会对颜色有偏好呢？

sentences.en: Um, so, you know, there's this potential that color has to, to do a lot of things in the brain.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你知道，颜色在大脑中发挥作用的潜力是巨大的。

sentences.en: Um, and much of these happen at this base on conscious level before cognition, before we can even perceive what's happening, which is why we have a hard time
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中大部分作用发生在认知之前的基本意识层面，甚至在我们感知到发生了什么之前，这就是为什么我们很难

sentences.en: understanding what they are, um, or even believing that they're there.
sentences.zh: 去理解它们是什么，嗯，甚至很难相信它们的存在。

sentences.en: So, you know, from an evolutionary perspective, this impact of color on trauma and psychology can be explained by this
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，从进化论的角度来看，颜色对创伤和心理的影响可以用我们提出的这个

sentences.en: principle of biophilia that we suggest, um, you know, or biophilia says that humans have a, this natural tendency to try and connect with nature or compare themselves to nature.
sentences.zh: 亲生命性原则来解释，嗯，你知道，或者说亲生命性理论认为人类有一种与生俱来的倾向，试图与自然建立联系或将自己与自然进行比较。

sentences.en: And then as we move further away from nature or natural, uh, principles, we become more healthy.
sentences.zh: 而当我们离自然或自然原则越远，我们的健康状况就会越差。

sentences.en: And that doesn't mean that you shouldn't cook your food and you should go on a paleo diet and only eat nuts.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说你不应该做饭，或者你应该去吃原始饮食，只吃坚果。

sentences.en: It means that we've kind of evolved to do certain specific things for a reason.
sentences.zh: 它的意思是，我们进化出某些特定的行为是有原因的。

sentences.en: They kept us alive.
sentences.zh: 它们让我们得以生存。

sentences.en: And the more you try and bend human nature away from those things, the more problems happen now, you know, politically or
sentences.zh: 你越是试图扭曲人性，使其背离这些本能，现在出现的问题就越多，你知道，在政治上或

sentences.zh: 哲学上，或者文化上，你会因为什么是自然的、什么不是而产生争论。

sentences.en: So I'm not, that's not what I'm trying to say.
sentences.zh: 所以我不是，我并不是想表达那个意思。

sentences.en: I'm not trying to argue for any sort of political position.
sentences.zh: 我并不是在为任何政治立场辩护。

sentences.en: What I'm saying is just that the more that you make people do things that they were not designed to do, um, the harder it is for them to do those things.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，你越是强迫人们去做他们本性之外的事情，嗯，他们做这些事情就越困难。

sentences.en: Some maybe are good things that we should do.
sentences.zh: 有些可能是我们应该做的好事。

sentences.en: And then some maybe are bad things that we should not.
sentences.zh: 而有些可能是不该做的坏事。

sentences.en: I mean, one example, I think when you get into huge scale systems, um, like something like climate change, um, you are looking
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，举个例子，我认为当你进入大规模系统时，嗯，比如气候变化这类事情，嗯，你面对的是

sentences.en: at something that is so big and so complicated and so many balls have to hit the next thing that we
sentences.zh: 一个如此庞大、如此复杂，且环环相扣的问题，以至于我们

sentences.en: And then beyond that, we have to rely on something like equations or, or, um, you know, spreadsheets or, you know, these things that keep track of complex logic for us.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，我们就必须依赖方程式、或者，嗯，你知道，电子表格，或者，你知道，这些能为我们追踪复杂逻辑的东西。

sentences.en: You know, AI is a pretty good example because what AI is doing is it's, it's using the statistical engine to grab all these things on the internet.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人工智能就是一个很好的例子，因为人工智能所做的，就是利用统计引擎去抓取互联网上的所有信息。

sentences.en: A ton of times there's so many things that it grabs.
sentences.zh: 它抓取的东西多得惊人。

sentences.en: It doesn't even know why it thinks that, you know, there's a court case that was brought, uh, against
sentences.zh: 它甚至不知道自己为什么会那样认为，你知道，曾经有一场官司，呃，是针对

sentences.en: um, if somebody was going to be a recidivist, if they were going to offend after they were let out of prison again.

sentences.en: And it, you know, it was upheld.

sentences.en: Um, and neither does the AI there's just too much information going through there, but, um, it is right.

sentences.zh: 所以我们打算采纳它的建议。

sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，所以气候变化，我认为就是我所说的

sentences.en: I'm saying here.

sentences.en: Like that's maybe something where we should learn to do something.
sentences.zh: 那可能就是我们应该学习去应对的事情。

sentences.en: It's not terribly natural.
sentences.zh: 这并不是非常自然的事情。

sentences.en: Um, because we can't even understand the complexity of that issue and what it means enough to act on it because we're not designed to do that, do that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为我们甚至无法理解那个问题的复杂性及其含义，以至于无法采取行动，因为我们天生就不是为了处理这些而设计的。

sentences.en: Um, and it means that there could be pretty big catastrophic consequences if we don't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这意味着如果我们不这样做，可能会产生相当严重的灾难性后果。

sentences.en: Um, but, you know, evolutionary psychology and archetypal theory, they propose that certain colors have this deep
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，你知道，进化心理学和原型理论提出，某些颜色具有根深蒂固的

sentences.en: rooted symbolic meaning and they can evoke this archetypal response within you.
sentences.zh: 象征意义，它们可以在你内心唤起这种原型反应。

sentences.en: And these archetypes are thought to be universal and inherited and represent fundamental human experiences and emotions.
sentences.zh: 这些原型被认为是普遍且遗传的，代表了基本的人类经验和情感。

sentences.en: Um, but for example, you know, red can evoke passion or danger or energy and blue may illicit calmness and tranquility and even sadness.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但举个例子，你知道，红色可以唤起激情、危险或能量，而蓝色可能会引起平静、安宁，甚至悲伤。

sentences.en: And these archetypal associations with colors have developed over time as adaptive responses to the environment.
sentences.zh: 这些与颜色的原型联想是随着时间的推移，作为对环境的适应性反应而形成的。

sentences.en: So, um, to talk about that ETT therapy, just real fast, you know, it's use of specific colors and hypothetical mechanisms,
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，简单谈谈那个ETT疗法，你知道，它对特定颜色和假设机制的使用，

sentences.en: um, can be derived, you know, both, you can look at them, you know, from a Jungian or evolutionary
sentences.zh: 嗯，可以追溯，你知道，你可以从荣格或进化论的

sentences.en: standpoint, but ETT uses this set of color filters that influence emotional states and facilitate therapeutic transformation.
sentences.zh: 角度来看待它们，但ETT使用了一套色彩滤镜，可以影响情绪状态并促进治疗性的转变。

sentences.en: And from an evolutionary perspective, those colors and light directions that ETT is using, they may tap into these primal associations with where the sun is and what angle
sentences.zh: 从进化论的角度来看，ETT所使用的那些颜色和光线方向，可能触及了我们对太阳位置以及它照射角度的原始联想，

sentences.en: it's coming from and, um, what color things are.
sentences.zh: 以及，嗯，事物的颜色。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, that's probably where they come from.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道，这可能就是它们的来源。

sentences.en: I don't think that our brain decided to do something that complicated at random and I've seen it have some pretty profound effects.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们的大脑会随机决定做如此复杂的事情，而且我亲眼见过它产生了一些非常深远的影响。

sentences.en: So, you know, for instance, using, you know, calming shades of green or blue might activate this connection with natural landscapes and trigger
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，例如，使用，你知道，平静的绿色或蓝色调可能会激活这种与自然景观的联系，并触发

sentences.en: relaxation responses and potentially reduce stress or trauma related symptoMs. And then from a Jungian
sentences.zh: 放松反应，并可能减轻压力或与创伤相关的症状。然后从荣格的

sentences.en: standpoint, the colors employed in ETT, um, they might be chosen based on their archetypal symbolism.
sentences.zh: 角度来看，ETT中采用的颜色，嗯，可能是根据它们的原型象征意义来选择的。

sentences.en: For example, like warm colors, like red or orange could be utilized to activate this archetype of vitality or energy.
sentences.zh: 例如，像红色或橙色这样的暖色调，可以用来激活这种活力或能量的原型。

sentences.en: Um, and a lot of like chromo therapies that came out in the seventies, they did this, you know, some of them, uh, are a little bit crankier than others.
sentences.zh: 嗯，七十年代出现的很多色彩疗法，它们确实做了这些，你知道，其中一些，呃，比其他的要更古怪一些。

sentences.en: Like they would say, like, you know, to, to be brave before you go into the interview, look at the color blue or something.
sentences.zh: 比如他们会说，你知道，在去面试之前为了变得勇敢，看看蓝色之类的东西。

sentences.en: And, um, generally those have kind of fallen out of favor.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，通常那些方法已经不再流行了。

sentences.en: If you think that that's what ETT is, it's not, um, ETT, uh, is using very specific frequencies and light directions, um, to get a pretty profound reaction.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为ETT就是那种东西，那不是，嗯，ETT，呃，使用的是非常特定的频率和光线方向，嗯，以获得相当深远的反应。

sentences.en: Like I said, I watched the color blue turn black in front of me and I'm looking at a piece of paper, but it's looking like a computer screen that can change color.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，我看着蓝色在我面前变成了黑色，我看着一张纸，但它看起来像是一个可以变色的电脑屏幕。

sentences.en: And I'm like, brain is like, why, why is this happening?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，大脑在想，为什么，为什么会发生这种情况？

sentences.en: So if you want to see the spectral chart, um, if you're a therapist in the area, come by the office.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想看光谱图，嗯，如果你是该地区的治疗师，欢迎来办公室。

sentences.en: So you can see what it's like and see if you want to get trained in it.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能看到它是什么样的，看看你是否想接受相关培训。

sentences.en: But now our brain filters these, this energy that we're talking about into five or, you know, some say six senses.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们的大脑将我们谈论的这种能量过滤成五种，或者，你知道，有人说是六种感官。

sentences.en: Um, but it's really, you know, just electrical impulses and energy that could be filtered together and, and, and influence each other on the space level before it's processed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但实际上，你知道，这只是电脉冲和能量，它们可以在被处理之前在空间层面上被过滤在一起，并相互影响。

sentences.en: So, you know, synesthesia is this intriguing thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，联觉是一种迷人的现象。

sentences.en: Um, you know, if you're an artist or you're a scientist and it provides this window into intricate workings of the brain on a pretty base level.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，如果你是一位艺术家或科学家，它提供了一个窗口，可以深入了解大脑在相当基础层面上的复杂运作。

sentences.en: Um, but synesthesia is not the way we think it's a byproduct of the way we think.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但联觉并不是我们思考的方式，它是我们思考方式的副产品。

sentences.en: And through understanding that, you know, we can understand ourselves and how to heal better, um,
sentences.zh: 通过理解这一点，你知道，我们可以了解自己以及如何更好地治愈，嗯，

sentences.zh: 并找到新的方法来欺骗大脑，释放所有，呃，储存在体内的创伤，而这正是创伤治疗师试图引导出来的。

sentences.en: You know, if there is a path to our future models of therapy, I think it's through looking at something like this or understanding the brain in this way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果通往我们未来治疗模式有一条路径，我认为就是通过观察类似这样的事物，或者以这种方式理解大脑。

sentences.en: So, you know, all of our senses come from this giant stew pot that the brain must filter, into specific ingredients afterward.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们所有的感官都来自这个巨大的炖锅，大脑必须在之后将其过滤成特定的成分。

sentences.en: It's not making a stew out of the ingredients.
sentences.zh: 它不是用这些成分做炖菜。

sentences.en: It's pulling ingredients out of a stew.
sentences.zh: 它是从炖菜中把成分挑出来。

sentences.en: Um, but they've already marinated and they've already influenced each other and the taste of one another is on them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但它们已经腌制过了，它们已经相互影响，彼此的味道都留在了对方身上。

sentences.en: There's some of the bone and the carrot and there's some of the onion and the olive or, you know, what that's a gross stew, but whatever.
sentences.zh: 里面有一些骨头、胡萝卜，还有一些洋葱和橄榄，或者，你知道，那是一锅糟糕的炖菜，但无所谓。

sentences.en: I mean, the stuff is steeped in each other and then we're pulling it out to perceive it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些东西浸泡在一起，然后我们把它们挑出来去感知它们。

sentences.en: And so I think by looking at that mechanism that, you know, what I see influences what I taste influences what I feel and influences what I say.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为通过观察那种机制，你知道，我所看到的会影响我所尝到的，影响我所感受到的，并影响我所说的。

sentences.en: And then of course, emotion is going to influence cognition, but emotion has already been colored by senses and the body before you even got to, um, mood and then

sentences.en: cognition comes last and a language-based thought comes laSt. Um, all this stuff has taken place

sentences.en: firSt. And, um, so if we're going to make a non-cognitive therapy that kind of goes deeper into the brain, this is the way I think about it.

sentences.en: And this is kind of an open-ended thought.

sentences.en: Um, but you know, accepting all the depth and complexity that's beneath cognition, I think can help us get a better sense of what makes us human.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但你知道，接受认知之下所有的深度和复杂性，我认为可以帮助我们更好地理解是什么让我们成为人类。
